note: The answer correctly states the low-pH compensation error and its ~50 percent magnitude but omits the hydrogen-ion conductance share the 'largest source of error' point the 25 °C equilibration check its pass bar and the comment-field recording requirement. Unmet: explains the cause as the hydrogen ion having different transport properties from other ions and contributing a large share of the conductance at low pH; states that at low pH the temperature correction can be the single largest source of error in the measurement; describes the check of comparing the in-situ reading against the same water equilibrated to 25 C; gives the pass bar for that check as within about 5 microsiemens per centimetre at or below 100 or about 3 percent above that; states that if an alternative low-pH compensation method is used the compensation factor has to be recorded in the comment field

The answer asserts the buffers are suitable for acidic water and never states that the 4/7/10 set is insufficient that the procedure covers pH 1.68–10 that the sample must fall in the calibrated range the ±10 °C buffer-temperature requirement or the ±0.05 pH unit check so it misses every must-contain point. Unmet: States the usual 4/7/10 buffer set is not sufficient for acidic water and a pH 1.68 (or 2) buffer is needed; States the standard pH procedure is expected to be accurate over roughly pH 1.68 to 10; States the sample pH must fall inside the calibrated range so a 4/7/10 set does not bracket pH 3.2; States the calibration buffers must be within about 10 C of the sample temperature; States a check of the buffer nearest the sample pH should be within about 0.05 pH unit of its value at that temperature or the system is recalibrated

Unmet: Explains bailed/decanted samples cannot establish unqualified ambient Eh; acknowledges subsample section permits estimated explicitly qualified reporting; States ORP DO and temperature are required to be measured in situ where possible while pH conductivity and turbidity are only recommended to be; States that in anoxic or reducing groundwater subsample procedures must not be used at all unless handled under an inert gas; Warns that a peristaltic or other suction-lift pump also must not be used for ORP or DO because negative pressure volatilises dissolved gases

The answer correctly gives the thermal-equilibration time (>30 min) the 15–20 min then ~10 min reading schedule and the ±5 mV tolerance but omits the in-situ/airtight-system requirement tubing impermeability and purging the ORP-vs-pH response asymmetry the nearest-10-mV reporting of calculated Eh and the electrode system to be logged. The answer makes only the temperature-change-during-transport point addressing temperature bias rather than the turbidity bench-measurement biases (condensation cell orientation coloured water gas bubbles dirty cells) the rubric asks for and it does not require checking both methods. The answer gives the subsample-qualifier idea but only for temperature (not turbidity DO or Eh) and it refuses the flow-cell sampling question instead of stating the prohibition so it misses the turbidity-specific qualifier the flow-cell prohibition and the storage/time-sensitivity points. The answer gives the 60-second equilibration and the median-of-final-readings points but never states that the value recorded at each vertical is the median of values observed within about 60 seconds after equilibration. The answer correctly states no conversion is needed since mho and siemens are the same unit but omits the 1971 changeover the synonymous terminology and the temperature-reference caveat.
